Chapter 7: The Influence of Environment and Relationships
Have you ever noticed how the people and places around you can totally change the way you feel and act? No one really makes it on their own. The folks we spend time with, the spaces we live and work in, and even our culture—they all shape our mindset and the outcomes we see in life.
Let’s dig into how your environment and relationships can be your biggest supporters... or your toughest obstacles when it comes to building a positive attitude.
Think of your environment as both a mirror and a mold. It reflects who you are right now, but it also helps shape who you'll become. When you’re in a space that supports you, it’s just so much easier to stick with good habits and keep a positive outlook. But if you’re surrounded by negativity, even the strongest willpower can start to crumble.
So, how do you stack the odds in your favor? Here are a few practical ways:
First, choose your associations wisely. Spend more time with people who lift you up, challenge you, and push you to grow.
Next, limit your exposure to negativity. If there are people who drain your energy or always seem to reinforce your doubts, it’s okay to step back a little.
Don’t forget your physical environment, either. You can set up reminders for yourself—maybe a vision board with your goals, a favorite quote on your wall, or even just keeping your workspace organized. These little cues can keep you focused on what really matters.
And seek out communities that support your dreams. Whether it’s a club, a group, or an online network, being around like-minded people can make a world of difference.
Here’s a metaphor I love: think of yourself as a plant in a greenhouse. Plants thrive when they’re in the right environment, with just the right amount of light, water, and care. People aren’t so different. When you’re surrounded by encouragement, resources, and positive examples, you’ll flourish, too.
There are plenty of real-life stories that show how this works. Take a student who was struggling in school—once he joined a study group full of motivated friends, his grades shot up. Or the entrepreneur who felt stuck, but found new ideas and energy after going to a few industry meetups and connecting with mentors.
There’s another important piece here—it’s not just about what you get, but what you give. When you offer support, encouragement, and positivity to others, you actually reinforce those same attitudes within yourself. It creates this amazing cycle of growth that lifts everyone up.
Now, I get it—not everything in your environment is under your control. But even small changes can add up. Maybe it’s reaching out to someone new, or just rearranging your workspace to feel more inspiring. Over time, these tweaks can make a big difference.
So, here’s the key takeaway: environment and relationships are powerful tools for change. If you pay attention to them—shaping them in ways that support your growth—you’ll create the perfect ground for a positive mindset to take root... and really thrive.
